gloss: is nothing but; is none other than

definitions.gloss: is nothing but; is none other than; is precisely
definitions.explanation: Fixed pattern used to emphatically identify one thing as the sole or true essence of another. Frequently used in formal writing, essays, and speeches to make a definitive claim.

examples.japanese: {成功|せいこう}の{秘訣|ひけつ}は{努力|どりょく}にほかならない。
examples.english: The secret to success is nothing but effort.

examples.japanese: これは{我々|われわれ}の{勝利|しょうり}にほかならない。
examples.english: This is nothing less than our victory.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{言葉|ことば}は、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}に{勇気|ゆうき}を{与|あた}えた{真実|しんじつ}にほかならない。
examples.english: His words were none other than the truth that gave courage to many people.

notes:
Emphatic identifying pattern formed from に + {他|ほか}ならない (literally 'is not other than'). Used to insist that X is precisely Y, no other interpretation possible.

STRUCTURE:
- [noun] + にほかならない
- Often appears at the end of an explanatory sentence summing up a cause, identity, or essence.

REGISTER:
Formal and emphatic. Common in essays, editorials, academic writing, and speeches. In casual conversation, まさに〜だ or 〜こそ〜だ is more natural.

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- 〜にすぎない: is nothing more than — downplays the subject (negative emphasis)
- 〜こそ〜だ: ~ is precisely ~ — similar emphasis, less formal
- まさに〜だ: truly is ~ — adverbial emphasis, more conversational
